title: Measure numeric error
summary: Mean absolute error averages the size of prediction mistakes without keeping their plus or minus signs.
introduction: Mean absolute error averages the size of prediction mistakes without keeping their plus or minus signs. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Mean absolute error averages the size of prediction mistakes without keeping their plus or minus signs.
The result is 0.5. The absolute errors are 1 and 0, whose average is one half.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: The error is in the target's units; do not compare unrelated tasks without context.
